Dated this the 11th day of March, 2025 Petitioner is the 3rd accused in Crime No.164 of 2004 registered at the Shooranadu Police Station for offences punishable under Sections 406, 420,
120(B), 294B and 506(i) r/w Section 34 of IPC.
2.

After purchasing the bus,
accused failed to pay the balance amount and on the defacto 2025:KER:20476 complainant questioning the accused about their conduct, he was abused using obscene words and criminally intimidated.
On filing of final report, the case was numbered as C.C. No.934 of 2004 on the files of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Sasthamcotta.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Sasthamcotta
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: All accused, except petitioner, faced trial in the case and were acquitted by Annexure II judgment.
The petitioner is seeking to get the proceedings against him quashed on the strength of the judgment of acquittal rendered in the case of the other accused.
3. According to the learned Counsel for the petitioner, substratum of the prosecution is lost by the findings in Annexure II judgment.
Hence, no purpose will be served by continuing the prosecution against 2025:KER:20476 the petitioner.
In support of this argument, reference is made to paragraph Nos.9 and 10 of the judgment.
4. I heard the learned Public Prosecutor also.
5. As rightly contended, Annexure II judgment reveals that the prosecution had miserably failed to prove the charges levelled against the accused.
Although the 1st accused is stated to have purchased the defacto complainant's bus, registration certificate of the bus was not produced in evidence.
Like wise, the agreement based on which the bus was allegedly handed over to the accused was also not produced.
Moreover, as held by the trial court, non-payment of the amount due to the financier, will not attract Sections 406 and 420 of IPC.
No evidence to substantiate the allegations regarding commission of the offences under Sections 294(b) and 506 was let in 2025:KER:20476 by the prosecution.
Being so, continuance of the prosecution against the petitioner will be an empty formality, there being no chance of his conviction at the end of the trial.
